_meta.type: build -- absolute floor, then cross-sectional rank
_meta.plan: plan revision 2, incorporating Correction 1 (2026-09-21) in full
_meta.record_correction: The v2 brief states v1 'was never sent'. v1 was built, committed and pushed on 2026-09-18 (a97f06e, explore/relative-momentum-v1). Correction 1 accepted this both ways; v1's population and concurrency artifacts are reused.

architecture.order: ABSOLUTE FLOOR first, then CROSS-SECTIONAL RANK on survivors only
architecture.no_trade: if no candidate live at tau passes the floor, the system returns NO_TRADE. The v0/v1 design could not produce this outcome -- ranking always names a winner.
architecture.no_warmup: the floor references no historical distribution, so there is no burn-in and no first-N-observations-behave-differently regime. It works on day one, live.
architecture.source: pseudocode supplied 2026-09-21, implemented verbatim except for the price change below

floor_conditions.note: six conditions, all AND'd. price_too_low is NOT among them -- see price_filter.

no_depth.quantity: median (bid_size * bid + ask_size * ask), USD -- BOTH sides summed
no_depth.revision: Correction 1 section 4: decoupled from clip size. Tying it to a multiple of intended size assumed a capacity relationship that does not hold here -- SEC's small-cap study puts depth at 0.2-1.1% of mid-cap. In these names you fill across repeated refreshes, not off one displayed quote, so capacity is carried by thin_notional over the window and no_depth only confirms a two-sided book exists at all.
no_depth.guard: DEPTH_AVAILABLE -- an event with no usable quote in the window is not rejected on this condition; depth_available = FALSE is carried

price_filter.name: price_too_low
price_filter.quantity: last print price in window, USD
price_filter.status: PULLED OUT OF THE FLOOR AND (Correction 1 section 4)
price_filter.why: it rejects more than everything else combined and it is a COST decision, not an attention decision. Left inside the floor it masks every other condition's contribution and makes the fail-reason histogram unreadable.
price_filter.reporting: every policy is run BOTH WITH AND WITHOUT it

ladders._construction: round, log-spaced, positioned against the LEFT TAIL of the measured distribution (Correction 1 section 3). Swept ONE AT A TIME around the declared reference rung -- 13 distinct configurations, not 729. Read across; no rung is privileged. If a result exists only at one rung, the rung is the finding.
ladders._why_left_tail: the 903 candidates are all moments where the participation gate already fired, so the sample has already passed an implicit activity filter. Positioning rungs at p25 of THAT distribution is a second selection gate -- the exact mechanism that damaged v0 and v1. The floor's job is catching dead tape, not trimming the healthy distribution.

MAX_SPREAD_BP.note: NOT specified in Correction 1 section 3's table -- inferred from its principle and flagged for sign-off. A CEILING reaches degenerate cases from the RIGHT, so the left-tail logic inverts: sampled p95 was 476 bp, so these rungs reject roughly the worst 5% / 1% / ~0% rather than the ~25% a 200 bp ceiling would have taken.

build_time_assert.rule: no input to ABSOLUTE_FLOOR is divided by a prior-session baseline, a rolling mean of its own series, another candidate's value, or a percentile of any distribution
build_time_assert.implementation: research/relative_momentum_v2/common.py::assert_floor_inputs_absolute -- the floor is handed a whitelist of raw measured columns and raises if B_e, score, or any percentile/rank/ratio-derived column reaches it. Relative volume is structurally available to the ranker only.

spread_units.collinearity_note: spread in bp is price-normalised over a $0.12-$16.43 population. Above $1.00 the minimum increment is a penny (Rule 612), so a $2.28 name cannot quote tighter than ~44 bp, while a $0.12 name quotes on the $0.0001 sub-penny grid and can show 8 bp. The bp distribution is mechanically driven by price at the low end, so MAX_SPREAD_BP and MIN_PRICE are partly the same gate. Stated in the report.

exclude: bid_size or ask_size null or zero
quote_exclusions_d17.carry: locked (bid == ask) -- a real transient state with a genuine zero spread; dropping it biases measured spread upward
quote_exclusions_d17.no_event_excluded: no event is excluded on quote-quality grounds; coverage is carried as a covariate

population.reused_not_rebuilt: v1-T0's tick-exact reconstruction of the runner's gap gate, including queued entries and the next-tick fill convention, validated 6/6 against the run's own recorded entry_price
population.coverage_statement: 903 of 15,763 D1 events = 5.7%, val split 2023-11-17 to 2024-07-22. NOT a measurement over D1.
population.trade: gate's own: first-window rising-edge entry (gap-gated), window-close exit, realized hold

d1_concurrency_t2.headline: 27.9% of candidate moments carry a second live name at 9-min liveness (the gate's own median window), against 10.5% measured on the gate population; coverage 15,363/15,763 = 97.5%; the +30%-crossing proxy fires EARLIER than an EPG rising edge so every figure is an upper bound

ranker.name: relative_volume
ranker.baseline_status: UNCOMMITTED on explore/fundamental-e1. The FLOOR does not depend on it; only the ranker does.
ranker.liveness: [entry trigger ts, natural_exit_ts] of each candidate's own selected window

policies.A: baseline -- every first-window signal, no qualification
policies.R: rank only, no floor -- CONTROL, deliberately reproduces the broken v0 case
policies.F+R: floor, then rank survivors -- the proposal
policies.F+R contested: F+R where ranking actually chose among >= 2 survivors

calibration_gate_t1b.status: HARD STOP, not a formality (Correction 1 sections 5 and 6)
calibration_gate_t1b.gate_5b: if a reference rung lands above p10 on the full 903, it is still a selection gate -- report and STOP
calibration_gate_t1b.gate_5c: split all seven quantities by session segment and confirm the degenerate dead-tape cases are present in the left tail. If absent from the 903, the floor cannot be calibrated against its own purpose and v2 STOPS -- the exercise would be blind.
calibration_gate_t1b.gate_6: project survivor and contested counts at all 13 configurations BEFORE T2 runs. STOP if the F+R contested cell is too small to read. v0's was 42 of 244.
calibration_gate_t1b.contested_floor_n_note: the config's own display floor. A declared round number, not fitted.

cost.native_model: none -- the gate has no fill or cost model; verified in v0-T3 (pnl is a pure price ratio, config/strategy.json has no fee block)

constraints.move_at: never momentum_pct, in any threshold, score or slice
constraints.d4: tick-derived only; no spine numeric column enters any computed quantity

predictions_recorded_before_the_run.note: Correction 1 section 7, replacing the first draft's. Recorded so they can be checked rather than rationalised afterwards.
predictions_recorded_before_the_run.1: the floor rejects a SMALL MINORITY, not a large share
predictions_recorded_before_the_run.2: single_venue rejects almost nobody (sampled p5 was 3 venues)
predictions_recorded_before_the_run.3: the binding condition is whichever of thin_notional / too_few_prints catches the premarket dead-tape cases
predictions_recorded_before_the_run.4: if the floor still rejects a large share after this correction, the rungs are still too high and the histogram names which one
